key_insight: DBMol uses structure-prediction models as an optimization signal to design new small molecules that are both high-affinity and pocket-specific.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical generative pipeline for de novo ligand design, combining gradient-based improvement with chemical validity projection.
method: Start from an initial molecule and optimize its structure in a continuous space using pocket-specific interaction and affinity scores from a structure predictor.
Project the optimized molecular graph back to a discrete, chemically valid molecule with a flow-matching model.
Iterate optimization and projection to produce diverse candidate ligands without reference-ligand supervision.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong improvement on the Boltz-2 affinity proxy, better pocket coverage than unconditional generation, and competitive held-out AF3-based evaluation.
watch_item: Because the optimization is guided by predictor outputs, self-confirmation bias and model-locked errors remain a concern, especially if the evaluator and optimizer share similar inductive biases.
paper_title: DBMol: Design of High-Affinity, Target-Specific Small Molecules through Structure Prediction Models
